column1: # Retrospective validation set, version 1 — TARGETS
# Proteins whose expression in a yeast host is documented in a published
# campaign that states what was engineered. Assembled 2026-11-06 from PubMed.
# Every accession was resolved against the UniProt REST API; every pmid and doi
# comes from the PubMed record, not from memory.
# WHY THIS SET LOOKS LOPSIDED, ON PURPose
# reports/03-validation-set-feasibility.md concluded that successes test recall
# while only DIFFERENTIAL cases test discrimination, and that the set should be
# built around them deliberately. 11 of the 18 rows below belong to a
# differential or negative result: the same modification helped one protein and
# not another, or helped nothing at all. Those are the rows that can falsify the
# chassis rather than flatter it.
# CASE TYPES
#   differential_helped      paired with a protein the same modification did NOT help
#   differential_not_helped  the other half of such a pair
#   negative                 the modification did not help, or actively hurt
#   success                  campaign reports a modification that worked
# pair_id links the two halves of a differential pair, or the members of a
# negative panel tested together in one experiment.
# EXCLUDED, AND WHY — recorded so the set's gaps are visible
#   Hydrophobic cutinase mutant CY028 (pmid 9435084). The paper's differential is
#     wild-type versus a hydrophobic point-mutant of the SAME protein, which is
#     the sharpest possible test of our hydropathy heuristics. The mutant has no
#     UniProt accession and the abstract does not give the substitutions, so its
#     sequence cannot be reconstructed. Its wild-type partner is included.
#   Bivalent anti-CD3 immunotoxin (pmid 16151122). A fusion construct with no
#     single accession.
#   Architecturally similar scFv pair (recorded in protocol/scope-proteins-v1.md).
#     No PubMed record was resolved for it in this pass.
